play_name: Let your guard down in small steps to see who is safe
behavioral_target: Keeping your guard up all the way, with everyone, as a fixed rule.
trigger: You are getting to know someone new. You feel the pull to stay closed off so you won't get used again.
old_play: You keep your guard up fully, no matter what the person does.
function_of_old_play: Staying guarded keeps you feeling safe from being used or hurt again.
new_play: Notice when your guard is up. Let it down a little in small, safe ways. Then watch how the person treats you before you open more.
what_to_expect: Opening up even a little may feel scary. You might feel unsure for a while. You may find out someone is safe, or that they are not.
why_supports_task: It helps you tell safe people from unsafe people by watching what they actually do over time. That is the work of Discernment.
maintaining_behaviors_consolidated: Keeping your guard up so you don't get taken advantage of again (STM-1085)
context_limitations: If someone has shown they hurt you, or your safety is at risk, keep your guard up. This is only for people who have not shown they are unsafe.
review_reason: Built from one Context-Dependent behavior. Guardedness can be healthy pacing or a pattern-maintaining wall; the play stays conditional so it only applies where the person has not shown they are unsafe.
